Allow remote client management

Requires TAP and a management password. When enabled, listens on all network interfaces. Use an existing encrypted VPN path. Changing this switch or password ends the running TAP session. Reconnect to apply the new settings.
Available only with TAP. You may configure it while disconnected; doing so does not start the VPN.
Set remote management password
Use 12–128 visible ASCII characters, without spaces. The password fields are never restored or prefilled. Only the SHA-0 hash used by the SoftEther management protocol is stored.

Connect from a computer
Current Wi-Fi / virtual adapter addresses, TCP 9930, and VPN Client Manager / vpncmd instructions. Management RPC does not provide TLS.
No current Wi-Fi or virtual adapter address is available. Connect to Wi-Fi or establish the VPN first.

Current phone network endpoints (TCP 9930; for reference):
%1$s

Enable remote management and start the TAP management service first. The core can be running without a VPN connection; an open management port is not a connected VPN.

Windows: open SoftEther VPN Client Manager and choose “Manage SoftEther VPN Client on a Separate Computer”. In the host field, enter only a reachable phone Wi-Fi or virtual adapter IP, without a port. Use your remote management password. Use Client Manager, not VPN Server Manager.

Command line:
vpncmd PHONE_IP /CLIENT
For IPv6, use the raw IPv6 address without square brackets. Do not append :9930 to the host: vpncmd selects the management port. Enter the password when prompted, rather than adding it to the command.

The SoftEther management protocol does not use TLS encryption. Prefer the phone’s VPN address over an existing encrypted VPN path, and only enable access on a trusted network. Direct Wi-Fi/LAN management is not encrypted by this protocol. The computer must have a route to the selected phone IP.

The endpoint list reflects current interfaces; it does not test connectivity or confirm that the core is listening. Do not paste the full endpoint into the client host field; use only its IP.

SoftEther documentation: https://www.softether.org/4-docs/1-manual/4/4.7
